2026-11-07.headline: SharePoint site skills guide now details creation, permissions, and lifecycle controls
2026-11-07.overview: The period brought one documentation update for Copilot in SharePoint. The revised guidance explains how site owners manage site skills from Settings > Site skills, including their storage, ownership, permissions, and lifecycle operations.
2026-11-07.adminImpact: Site owners can use the documented management page and controls to administer site skills. No action is required.

keyChanges.title: Site skills management guidance expanded
keyChanges.detail: The Copilot in SharePoint article now documents creating and managing site skills from Settings > Site skills, including uploading, editing, enabling, disabling, copying, restoring, downloading, and deleting them. It also clarifies storage, ownership, and permissions.

2026-11-09.headline: Sensitivity-labeled PDFs gain web annotation in OneDrive and SharePoint in January 2027
2026-11-09.overview: OneDrive for Business and SharePoint on the web are scheduled to let users with editing rights annotate sensitivity-label protected PDFs without removing their labels. Saved files will retain both annotations and protections, with worldwide rollout planned for late January 2027.
2026-11-09.adminImpact: No admin action is required. Administrators should note that the capability applies only to OneDrive for Business and SharePoint and is intended for users with editing rights.

keyChanges.title: Editing rights will include annotation of protected PDFs
keyChanges.detail: Users with editing rights will be able to annotate sensitivity-label protected PDFs on the web without removing the labels. Annotations and protections will be preserved when the file is saved; worldwide rollout is planned for late January 2027.

2026-11-10.headline: Teams events will share OneDrive videos directly without screen sharing
2026-11-10.overview: The period’s main product update is a planned Microsoft Teams events capability that lets organizers and producers share OneDrive videos through “Manage what attendees see.” A separate SharePoint app-bar guidance update adds detail on navigation features, requirements, Teams integration, and rollout timing.
2026-11-10.adminImpact: No action is required for the OneDrive video-sharing rollout, which begins in mid-November 2026. Administrators configuring global navigation should review the updated guidance for permissions, Teams integration, user access expectations, and the possible 24-hour rollout delay.

keyChanges.title: OneDrive video sharing in Teams events
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Teams will let event organizers and producers share videos directly from OneDrive using “Manage what attendees see,” avoiding screen sharing or embedding videos in PowerPoint and supporting smoother, higher-quality playback. Rollout begins in mid-November 2026, with no action required.

keyChanges.title: Global navigation guidance adds feature and rollout detail
keyChanges.detail: The SharePoint app-bar setup page now describes personalized favorites and recents, quick access to Discover, Publish, Build, and OneDrive, and clarifies global-navigation requirements, permissions, Teams integration, and the possible 24-hour rollout delay.
keyChanges.product: SharePoint app bar and global navigation

2026-11-11.headline: App Intelligence access reviews documented alongside revised Trim Versions guidance
2026-11-11.overview: The November 11 period was documentation-led: Microsoft added a SharePoint governance article describing how administrators can prioritize and investigate non-Microsoft application access, and revised Trim Versions guidance with clearer operational limits and procedures.
2026-11-11.adminImpact: Administrators assessing application access can use the new workflow, although availability, roles, licensing, and assessment data depend on the tenant and release; the article requires no action. Before trimming versions, review the What-if guidance: deleted versions bypass the recycle bin and cannot be recovered unless previously backed up.

keyChanges.title: New workflow covers non-Microsoft application access investigations
keyChanges.detail: The new SharePoint article explains how administrators can prioritize and investigate application access using permissions, site reach, behavior evidence, and privileged-access information. Availability, required roles, licensing, and assessment data vary by tenant and release.

keyChanges.title: Trim Versions guidance now emphasizes the 30-day minimum
keyChanges.detail: The revised article identifies SharePoint Administrators as able to queue trim jobs, simplifies What-if and manual-expiration guidance, highlights the 30-day minimum, and removes the previous text about versions created before January 1, 2023.

2026-11-12.headline: App Intelligence guidance now details owner-notification preview and audit-data coverage
2026-11-12.overview: SharePoint had one documentation update: the App Intelligence access-review article now explains its use of application permissions and activity, an owner-notification preview and confirmation workflow, audit-data coverage, and reporting delays.
2026-11-12.adminImpact: Before sending owner notifications, administrators should review the recipients and message content. They should also account for the documented audit-data coverage and reporting delays when interpreting access-review results.

keyChanges.title: App Intelligence access-review guidance expands workflow and reporting details
keyChanges.detail: The updated SharePoint article describes App Intelligence as using application permissions and activity, adds an owner-notification preview and confirmation workflow, and documents audit-data coverage and reporting delays. Administrators should review recipients and message content before sending notifications and consider the stated data coverage when interpreting results.

2026-11-13.headline: SharePoint temporary authentication URLs retire on April 1, 2027
2026-11-13.overview: The main administrator deadline is the retirement of SharePoint temporary authentication URLs, which will break dependent Power Apps and Automate functionality. Separately, new guidance documents a tenant-level control for restricting agentic users from sharing SharePoint and OneDrive content externally.
2026-11-13.adminImpact: Review Power Apps and Automate functionality that relies on SharePoint temporary authentication URLs before April 1, 2027. For agentic sharing, the documented policy is off by default; administrators can enable it through SharePoint Online PowerShell and scope it to all agentic users or users associated with selected application blueprints, including first- or third-party applications.

keyChanges.title: Power Platform dependencies face a retirement deadline
keyChanges.detail: A Microsoft 365 Message Center notice says SharePoint temporary authentication URLs will be retired on April 1, 2027. Power Apps and Automate functionality that relies on these URLs will break when they are retired, so administrators should review those dependencies ahead of the deadline.

keyChanges.title: Tenant policy restricts agentic external sharing
keyChanges.detail: New Microsoft Learn guidance describes a tenant-level policy for SharePoint and OneDrive that blocks agentic users from sharing content with external users. The policy is off by default and can be enabled through SharePoint Online PowerShell for all agentic users or for users associated with selected application blueprints.

2026-11-14.headline: Large-scale Teams events will add direct OneDrive video sharing via “Manage what attendees see”
2026-11-14.overview: The period’s main operational change is an upcoming Teams events capability that lets organizers and producers share OneDrive videos directly, avoiding screen sharing or PowerPoint embedding. Microsoft also says newly created Copilot Pages and Notebooks will be stored in OneDrive for Business, while updated OneDrive release notes document November builds and syncing behavior during Windows Game Mode.
2026-11-14.adminImpact: No mandatory configuration change or user action is stated. Administrators should inform event staff and update event guidance for direct OneDrive video sharing, account for OneDrive governance and compliance controls applying to newly created Copilot Pages and Notebooks, and use the updated sync notes for rollout tracking and user messaging.

keyChanges.title: Direct OneDrive video sharing is coming to large-scale Teams events
keyChanges.detail: Organizers and producers will be able to use “Manage what attendees see” to share videos directly from OneDrive, providing playback without screen sharing or embedding in PowerPoint. Rollout starts in mid-November 2026; Microsoft recommends informing event staff and updating guidance, with no required action.

keyChanges.title: New Copilot Pages and Notebooks will be stored in OneDrive for Business
keyChanges.detail: Starting in mid-October 2026, newly created Microsoft 365 Copilot Pages and Notebooks will use OneDrive for Business storage. Existing files remain unchanged, while governance, compliance, data protection, retention, and lifecycle-management features apply to the new files; no user action is required.

keyChanges.title: OneDrive release notes record November builds and Game Mode sync pauses
keyChanges.detail: The updated release notes add November 2026 OneDrive builds, state that syncing pauses during Windows Game Mode and resumes afterward, and list reliability and performance fixes for recent Windows and macOS releases. No configuration change is stated.

2026-11-16.headline: New Copilot Pages and Notebooks will be stored in OneDrive for Business
2026-11-16.overview: Starting in mid-October 2026, newly created Microsoft 365 Copilot Pages and Notebooks are stored in OneDrive for Business. This brings the content under existing governance, compliance, data protection, retention, and lifecycle management controls, while existing Copilot content remains unchanged.
2026-11-16.adminImpact: No user action is required. Administrators can rely on existing OneDrive for Business governance, compliance, protection, retention, and lifecycle controls for newly created Copilot Pages and Notebooks.

keyChanges.title: New Copilot content uses OneDrive for Business storage
keyChanges.detail: The change applies to newly created Microsoft 365 Copilot Pages and Notebooks beginning in mid-October 2026. Existing Copilot content is unchanged, and newly created content gains coverage from OneDrive for Business governance, compliance, data protection, retention, and lifecycle management.

2026-11-17.headline: SharePoint agents begin requiring upgrades as OneDrive shifts to cloud.microsoft URLs
2026-11-17.overview: Two updates carry the most operational weight. The SharePoint and OneDrive agent upgrade experience begins rolling out in mid-November 2026, and existing .agent files used in Teams or Microsoft Copilot will stop responding until upgraded. Separately, OneDrive URLs are transitioning from contoso-my.sharepoint.com to onedrive.cloud.microsoft between September 2026 and September 2027. The other changes are primarily guidance and maintenance: Application Restrictions cmdlet availability is still rolling out, Viva Connections home-site management is directed to the SharePoint admin center, sharing-link guidance is more precise, and OneDrive Sync release notes add two production builds.
2026-11-17.adminImpact: Inventory affected agents and plan upgrades; Teams chats require all agents to be upgraded together, followed by replacing the old agent and verifying user access to the agent and its knowledge sources. For the OneDrive URL transition, review custom solutions and administrator documentation, but no immediate action is required because both domains will coexist and file access and APIs are unchanged. Use the SharePoint admin center for current home-site management, account for tenant differences in Application Restrictions cmdlet availability, and use the updated PowerShell module links. Sync administrators can use builds 26.204.1019.0009 and 26.212.1029.0006 when tracking deployments.

keyChanges.title: Agent upgrades will affect existing Teams and Copilot .agent files
keyChanges.detail: The upgrade experience begins rolling out in mid-November 2026. Existing .agent files used in Teams or Microsoft Copilot will stop responding until upgraded. Teams chats require upgrading all agents together, and the SharePoint Agents icon and Main agent setting will be removed.

keyChanges.title: OneDrive URLs transition from SharePoint domains to cloud.microsoft
keyChanges.detail: The transition from contoso-my.sharepoint.com to onedrive.cloud.microsoft starts in September 2026 and completes by September 2027. Both domains will coexist indefinitely, with no change to file access or APIs. Administrators should review custom solutions and documentation; no immediate action is required.

keyChanges.title: Application Restrictions guidance flags tenant-dependent cmdlet availability
keyChanges.detail: The Application Restrictions cmdlets are rolling out and may not yet be available in every tenant. The page also updates all listed PowerShell links to the Microsoft.Online.SharePoint.PowerShell module path.

keyChanges.title: Viva Connections home-site management is directed to SharePoint admin center
keyChanges.detail: Current setup guidance sends administrators to SharePoint admin center > Settings > Home sites to add, order, assign audiences to, and remove home sites. The Microsoft 365 admin center remains available as a legacy experience during the transition.

keyChanges.title: Shareable-link guidance separates direct access from link-based sharing
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance distinguishes direct access from link-based sharing and covers hero links, audience scopes, forwarding, authentication, and access through search or Copilot. It gives administrators clearer material for evaluating internal, guest, and anonymous sharing scopes.

2026-11-02.headline: Unified Copilot Search and group-permission governance reporting headline SharePoint administration
2026-11-02.overview: Two Message Center announcements carry the period: SharePoint Online and OneDrive for the web are moving to a unified Copilot Search experience, with preview rollout beginning in mid-October 2026 and general rollout in mid-January 2027; SharePoint’s Data access governance report for group permissions is scheduled to roll out worldwide from late November to early December. A separate Agents and Copilot article now documents the full site-skills management workflow.
2026-11-02.adminImpact: Copilot Search requires minimal organizational action, and users can opt out during preview. Administrators can use the forthcoming report in the admin center to find sites accessible to particular groups and assess access levels, supporting permission reviews and checks for unintended content exposure. Site owners can administer skills from Settings > Site skills using the documented controls; the article states that no action is required.

keyChanges.title: Copilot Search unifies SharePoint Online and OneDrive web search
keyChanges.detail: The updated experience adds natural-language prompts, AI summaries, and filters. The announced schedule places preview rollout from mid-October 2026 and general rollout from mid-January 2027; users can opt out during preview and organizational action is minimal.
keyChanges.product: SharePoint Online and OneDrive for the web

keyChanges.title: Data access governance report adds group-permission visibility
keyChanges.detail: The new report in the SharePoint admin center will help administrators identify sites accessible to specific groups and assess their access levels. Worldwide rollout is scheduled from late November to early December 2026, supporting permission management and efforts to prevent unintended content exposure.

keyChanges.title: Site skills management is documented under Settings > Site skills
keyChanges.detail: The updated article explains how to create and manage site skills, including uploading, editing, enabling, disabling, copying, restoring, downloading, and deleting them. It also clarifies storage, ownership, and permissions, giving site owners a documented management path.

2026-11-09.headline: SharePoint temporary authentication URLs retire April 1, 2027, breaking dependent Power Apps and Automate
2026-11-09.overview: An April 1, 2027 retirement will break Power Apps and Automate functionality that relies on SharePoint temporary authentication URLs. The period also brings documented controls for blocking agentic-user external sharing, an opt-in storage-overage meter, and OneDrive storage for newly created Copilot Pages and Notebooks. A January rollout adds protected-PDF annotation without removing sensitivity labels.
2026-11-09.adminImpact: Treat April 1, 2027, as a deadline for identifying Power Apps and Automate dependencies on temporary authentication URLs. The agentic-sharing policy can be configured through SharePoint Online PowerShell, while the opt-in storage meter requires Azure billing permissions. Newly created Copilot Pages and Notebooks will fall under OneDrive governance; the protected-PDF annotation rollout requires no admin action.

keyChanges.title: Temporary authentication URLs retire April 1, 2027
keyChanges.detail: Starting April 1, 2027, SharePoint temporary authentication URLs will be retired; the notice says Power Apps and Automate functionality that relies on them will break. Administrators should use the deadline to identify dependent scenarios.

keyChanges.title: Tenant policy can block agentic users from external sharing
keyChanges.detail: New guidance documents a tenant-level policy for SharePoint and OneDrive that is off by default. Administrators can enable it for all agentic users or only users associated with selected application blueprints, using SharePoint Online PowerShell, to keep agent-handled content internal.

keyChanges.title: Pay-as-you-go billing arrives for SharePoint storage overages
keyChanges.detail: An opt-in meter rolling out globally in January 2027 will charge only for SharePoint storage used beyond the included quota. It integrates with Microsoft 365 Archive and requires Azure billing permissions.

keyChanges.title: New Copilot Pages and Notebooks use OneDrive for Business storage
keyChanges.detail: Starting mid-October 2026, newly created Microsoft 365 Copilot Pages and Notebooks are stored in OneDrive for Business, allowing existing governance, compliance, data protection, retention, and lifecycle controls to apply. Existing files remain unchanged, and no user action is required.
keyChanges.product: OneDrive for Business and Microsoft 365 Copilot

keyChanges.title: Protected PDFs gain web annotation without removing sensitivity labels
keyChanges.detail: A worldwide rollout in late January 2027 will let users with editing rights annotate sensitivity-label-protected PDFs in OneDrive for Business and SharePoint on the web. Saving preserves both annotations and protections; no admin action is required.

2026-11-16.headline: SharePoint agent upgrades and OneDrive domain transition reshape admin planning
2026-11-16.overview: The week’s highest-impact changes affect behavior and administration: existing SharePoint agent files can stop responding until upgraded, OneDrive is transitioning to onedrive.cloud.microsoft, and SiteLogoUrl will no longer update automatically on individual search items. SharePoint is also set to enhance access-governance reports and site reviews in late November. Newly created Copilot Pages and Notebooks are being stored in OneDrive for Business under existing governance and compliance controls. Narrower documentation updates now direct Viva Connections administrators to SharePoint admin center > Settings > Home sites and add two November 13 OneDrive Production builds.
2026-11-16.adminImpact: Prioritize an inventory and upgrade plan for existing agents; Teams chats require all agents to be upgraded together, and access to their knowledge sources should be verified. Review custom solutions that depend on SiteLogoUrl or OneDrive hostnames, and update related documentation. The access-governance rollout requires preparation but no action before rollout; new Copilot storage requires no user action and uses existing OneDrive controls.

keyChanges.title: Existing SharePoint agents will stop responding until upgraded
keyChanges.detail: The upgrade experience begins rolling out in mid-November 2026. Existing .agent files used in Teams or Microsoft Copilot will stop responding until upgraded; Teams chats require all agents in the chat to be upgraded together. The SharePoint Agents icon and Main agent setting will be removed. Inventory affected agents, upgrade them, and verify access to their knowledge sources.

keyChanges.title: OneDrive URL transition runs through September 2027
keyChanges.detail: OneDrive is transitioning from contoso-my.sharepoint.com to onedrive.cloud.microsoft, starting September 2026 and completing by September 2027. Both domains will coexist indefinitely, while file access and APIs remain unchanged. Review custom solutions and update administrator documentation.

keyChanges.title: Enhanced SharePoint access-governance reports begin in late November
keyChanges.detail: The enhanced data access governance reports and site access reviews are intended to help administrators identify data risks, prioritize sites, direct review requests, and track email delivery. Rollout starts in late November 2026; no action is required before rollout, although administrators should prepare.

keyChanges.title: SiteLogoUrl stops automatic updates in SharePoint search metadata
keyChanges.detail: From December 2026 through March 2027, SharePoint will stop automatically updating the SiteLogoUrl property on individual items in search metadata. Solutions that use the property should retrieve logos directly from the site instead.

keyChanges.title: New Copilot Pages and Notebooks inherit OneDrive governance
keyChanges.detail: Starting mid-October 2026, newly created Microsoft 365 Copilot Pages and Notebooks are stored in OneDrive for Business, enabling existing governance, compliance, data protection, retention, and lifecycle management. Existing Copilot content remains unchanged, and no user action is required.

2026-11.headline: SharePoint authentication URL retirement sets April 1 deadline for dependent Power Apps
2026-11.overview: November’s most consequential changes include the April 1, 2027 retirement of SharePoint temporary authentication URLs, an agent-upgrade rollout that can stop existing .agent files from responding, and staged changes to SharePoint and OneDrive search and hosting. Administrators also need to account for SiteLogoUrl behavior changes and the transition to OneDrive’s cloud.microsoft domain.
2026-11.adminImpact: Inventory Power Apps and Power Automate dependencies on temporary authentication URLs before April 1, 2027. Identify existing agents and plan upgrades, including upgrading all agents together in affected Teams chats. Review custom solutions that use SiteLogoUrl or hard-code OneDrive hostnames, and update related documentation. Copilot Search requires minimal organizational action, with user opt-out available during preview.

keyChanges.title: Temporary SharePoint authentication URLs retire April 1, 2027
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft will retire SharePoint temporary authentication URLs on April 1, 2027. Power Apps and Power Automate functionality that relies on these URLs will break, making dependency identification and remediation the key administrator deadline.

keyChanges.title: Existing SharePoint agents must be upgraded to keep responding
keyChanges.detail: The upgrade experience begins rolling out in mid-November 2026. Existing .agent files used in Teams or Microsoft Copilot will stop responding until upgraded; Teams chats require all agents to be upgraded together. The SharePoint Agents icon and Main agent setting will also be removed.

keyChanges.title: Copilot Search unifies SharePoint and OneDrive web search
keyChanges.detail: The updated experience adds natural-language prompts, AI summaries, and filters across SharePoint Online and OneDrive on the web. Preview rollout starts in mid-October 2026, general rollout is planned for mid-January 2027, and users can opt out during preview.

keyChanges.title: SharePoint stops automatically updating SiteLogoUrl in search metadata
keyChanges.detail: During the December 2026 to March 2027 rollout, SharePoint will stop automatically updating the SiteLogoUrl property on individual search items. Solutions that use the property for search-result logos should retrieve logos directly from the site instead.

keyChanges.title: OneDrive transitions to the cloud.microsoft domain through September 2027
keyChanges.detail: OneDrive URLs will transition from contoso-my.sharepoint.com to onedrive.cloud.microsoft, starting in September 2026 and completing by September 2027. Both domains will coexist indefinitely, with no changes to file access or APIs; administrators should review custom solutions and update documentation.
